newsitem.title: DENMARK: SOCCER-GREEK OWN GOAL HELPS LUCKY DANES TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GREEK OWN GOAL HELPS LUCKY DANES TO VICTORY.

text.p: An own goal gift and a brilliant solo effort by Brian Laudrup propelled Denmark to a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Greece in a World Cup qualifying match on Wednesday.

A cross from Danish defender Thomas Helveg in the 25th minute was deflected off the boot of Theodoros Zagorakis past goalkeeper Ilias Atmatsidis, who could only look on helplessly as Denmark took a 1-0 lead in the group one encounter.
The Greek blunder brought life to a rather ragged Danish team. Minutes later striker Peter Nielsen rammed the ball into the Greek net only to have a goal disallowed for offside.
But Greece equalised 10 minutes after conceding the unfortunate own goal. Themistoclis Nicolaidis was brought down in a scuffle in front of the Danish goalmouth and won a free-kick.
Georgios Donis struck a powerful shot which pierced the Danish defensive wall as Peter Nielsen and Michael Laudrup ducked to avoid being hit and Greece were level.
But in the 50th minute Brian Laudrup scored a magnificent goal which proved sufficient to clinch Denmark's second win in group one following a 2-0 victory in Slovenia last month.
Laudrup, who plays for Scottish premier division Rangers, took off on a brilliant solo run through most of the Greek half and saw off four pursuers before ramming the ball into the net.
The Greeks put the Danish defence under considerable pressure after that and were unlucky not to equalise on several occasions.
"I am very happy about the win," Denmark's new Swedish-born coach Bo Johansson said.

"It was a very difficult match and we had problems with our defence. Anybody who thinks the Greeks are a walkover is silly but six points from our first two qualifiers is a strong start in the World Cup."
